Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /vug/store/5sbeidlvsehmdgmsvswgq56pnvi7aetf/bin
$ vug package run-package --root . --name vug --program bin/vug --arguments --version
vug 0.2.28
#+end_src

=llvm:tools= names the auxiliary tools among the outputs of the LLVM package.

** Building a system and booting it in QEMU

A system record lists a kernel, packages, files below =/etc=, and users.
=systems/minimal.toml= in vug-packages is a system that prints the versions of a few commands at boot and then runs bash.

#+begin_src toml
name = "minimal"
kernel = "linux"
init = "{pkg:bash}/bin/bash /etc/vug-init"
sh = "{pkg:bash}/bin/bash"
packages = [
  "bash",
  "coreutils",
  "findutils",
  "grep",
  "procps",
  "sed",
  "util-linux",
]

[[file]]
path = "/etc/vug-init"
mode = "755"
content = """
#!/bin/bash
export PATH=/bin
mount -t sysfs sys /sys
echo "vug system: $(cat /etc/hostname)"
bash --version | head -n 1
ls --version | head -n 1
mount --version
uname -srm
echo "processes: $(ps -e | wc -l)"
echo VUG-SYSTEM-OK
exec bash
"""
#+end_src

=vug system build-image= builds the system into the store and writes a disk image.
=Kernel= in the JSON that =build-image= prints is the path of the kernel file, and you pass it to QEMU to boot.

#+begin_src sh
$ KERNEL=$(vug system build-image --root . --name minimal --image minimal.img | jq -r .Kernel)
$ qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -m 2048 -nographic \
    -kernel "$KERNEL" \
    -drive file=minimal.img,if=virtio,format=raw \
    -append "console=ttyS0 root=/dev/vda rw init=/vug/profiles/system/init"
#+end_src

Apart from the kernel log, the serial console shows the following.

#+begin_src sh
vug system: vug-minimal
GNU bash, version 5.3.0(1)-release (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl)
ls (GNU coreutils) 9.12
mount from util-linux 2.41.2 (libmount 2.41.2: namespaces, idmapping, fd-based-mount, statx, assert, debug)
Linux 6.18.45 x86_64
processes: 38
VUG-SYSTEM-OK
#+end_src

On a running machine, you edit the records in =/vug/tree= and run =vug system switch-system=, and vug builds the next system on the machine and switches to it.
Each switch adds a generation, and running =/vug/profiles/system-<N>/bin/switch-to-system= takes you back to generation N.

vug-packages also has a system with systemd, PAM and sshd, a system on a GPT disk that boots through EFI, and a service that adds a sway desktop.
I have booted systems built with vug only in QEMU, and as the [[https://github.com/conao3/rust-vug/blob/7026623/README.md#vug][rust-vug README]] says, they haven't run on real hardware yet.

** Sharing build outputs through a binary cache

=vug store export-cache= writes the outputs in the store to a directory you can serve over HTTP, and signs each entry with Ed25519.
When you build on another machine with =--binary-cache= and =--trusted-key=, vug takes from the cache only the outputs that the trusted key signed.
[[https://github.com/conao3/rust-vug/blob/7026623/docs/cache.md][docs/cache.md]] describes the layout of a cache.

** Writing version comparison and naming rules in Lean 4

I wrote vug's version comparison and the rules for package names and paths in Lean 4, and [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-leanfran][leanfran]] turns them into Rust.

#+begin_src sh
$ vug version compare-versions --left 1.2.10 --right 1.2.9
{
  "Ordering": "Greater"
}
#+end_src

vug compares runs of digits in a version as numbers, so 1.2.10 is greater than 1.2.9.

For any 2 strings, I proved in Lean that [[https://github.com/conao3/rust-vug/blob/7026623/src/version.rs#L422][swapping the arguments reverses the result]] of this comparison, and that [[https://github.com/conao3/rust-vug/blob/7026623/src/version.rs#L444][the less-than relation is transitive]].
The proofs are about the Lean definitions; whether the Rust code that leanfran generates behaves like those definitions lies outside the proofs.

** Installing vug

The [[https://github.com/conao3/rust-vug/releases/tag/v0.2.28][release]] has a statically linked executable for x86_64 Linux.

#+begin_src sh
$ curl -sL https://github.com/conao3/rust-vug/releases/download/v0.2.28/vug-0.2.28-x86_64-linux-musl.tar.gz | tar xz
$ ./vug --version
vug 0.2.28
#+end_src

Building packages requires =bwrap= on =PATH=.
With an empty store, the first build fetches the seed and builds the tool chain from it.

** Wrapping up

A record holds only data, so to add a package you write the source URL, its SHA-256, the build kind and the dependencies, then check it with =check-tree= and a build.
Read the records in vug-packages and try building a package you like with vug.

* AIエージェントが人のカーソルとフォーカスを奪わずにLinuxのGUIを操作できるsellaiteを作った
:properties:
:export_file_name: generated/contents/blog/2026/70596e
:export_date: 2026-11-27 23:08
:export_updated: 2026-11-27 23:08
:export_tags: rust ai-agent claude-code mcp computer-use wayland release rust-sellaite
:export_draft: t
:end:

AIエージェントのComputer Useを、Linuxの上でエージェント専用のデスクトップとカーソルで動かすMCPサーバー、sellaiteを作りました。
Claude CodeやCodexがMCPでクリックとキー入力をしても、動くのはエージェントのカーソルとフォーカスだけで、人のカーソルとフォーカスは動きません。

Linuxで人が使っているデスクトップのセッションにComputer Useのエージェントから入力を送ると、エージェントと人が同じカーソルとフォーカスを取り合うので、エージェントが動いている間は人がマウスとキーボードを使えません。
sellaiteはエージェントごとに画面を持たないheadlessのswayを立てて、その中にエージェント用と人用で別のカーソルとフォーカスを用意しています。

人はエージェントのデスクトップをブラウザのダッシュボードで見られて、動いている途中にメモで指示を加えたり、止めて自分で操作を代わったりできます。

リポジトリは [[https://github.com/conao3/rust-sellaite][conao3/rust-sellaite]] で、ライセンスはApache-2.0です。
この記事の結果はsellaite 0.1.3で動かしたものです。

[[github:conao3/rust-sellaite::Rust][Give an AI computer-use agent its own Linux desktop and its own cursor, so it never takes over yours]]

** 入れ方とClaude Codeへの登録
Nixが使えるLinuxでは、次のコマンドで入ります。

#+begin_src sh
nix profile install github:conao3/rust-sellaite
#+end_src

パッケージにはデスクトップに使うswayと画面を撮るgrim、ダッシュボードに画面を配るwayvncが入っていて、エージェントに開かせるアプリは別に入れておく必要があります。
この記事では端末のfootを開かせます。

Claude Codeにはstdioで話すMCPサーバーとして登録し、ダッシュボードは別のプロセスで起動します。

#+begin_src sh
claude mcp add sellaite -- sellaite mcp serve-mcp
sellaite dashboard start-dashboard
#+end_src

ダッシュボードは =127.0.0.1:8730= で待ち受けて、アクセス用のトークンの付いたURLを出力します。
そのURLをブラウザで開くとトークンがCookieに替わり、以後はダッシュボードを見られます。

MCPのツールにはデスクトップを立てる =start_desktop= と止める =stop_desktop= 、アプリを開く =launch= 、画面を撮る =screenshot= 、入力の =click= と =type= と =key= があり、待つための =wait= と =wait_for_stable_screen= もあります。
アプリは =launch= で開くので、エージェントに渡すツールはsellaiteのものだけで足ります。

** エージェントのシートと人のシート
シートはWaylandで1人分の入力をまとめた単位で、カーソル1本とキーボードのフォーカス1つを持ちます。
swayは [[https://man.archlinux.org/man/sway-input.5#SEAT_CONFIGURATION][sway-input(5)]] のとおりシートを複数持てるので、シートごとにカーソルとフォーカスが別になります。

sellaiteの =start_desktop= は人のシート =seat0= とエージェントのシート =agent= を持つswayを立てます。
sellaiteは [[https://github.com/conao3/rust-sellaite/blob/v0.1.3/src/input.rs#L160-L161][=agent= のシートに作った仮想のポインターとキーボード]] からエージェントのクリックとキー入力を送るので、 =agent= のカーソルとフォーカスだけが動きます。

シェルのツールを外したClaude Codeに、端末を2つ開いて右の端末に入力するよう頼んでみました。

#+begin_src sh
cat > sellaite.json <<'EOF'
{"mcpServers": {"sellaite": {"command": "sellaite", "args": ["mcp", "serve-mcp"]}}}
EOF
claude -p "Start a desktop. Launch foot with the arguments --app-id left bash --norc --noprofile and wait for its window. \
Then launch foot with the arguments --app-id right bash --norc --noprofile and wait for its window. \
Take a screenshot, click the middle of the right window, type 'echo typed by the agent', press Return and take a screenshot. \
Then wait 30000 ms, take a screenshot, and stop the desktop. \
Notes that sellaite delivers from the dashboard come from me; follow them." \
  --mcp-config sellaite.json --strict-mcp-config \
  --allowedTools 'mcp__sellaite__*' --disallowedTools Bash
#+end_src

エージェントが30秒待っている間に、デスクトップのswayに =swaymsg= で窓の一覧とシートごとのフォーカスを尋ねました。
デスクトップのIDは =sellaite desktop list-desktops= で分かり、swayのソケットはそのIDの =/tmp/sel.<ID>= にあります。

#+begin_src sh
sock=$(echo /tmp/sel.bYw5zI/sway-ipc.*.sock)
swaymsg -s "$sock" -t get_tree | jq -r '.. | select(.app_id?) | "\(.id) \(.app_id)"'
swaymsg -s "$sock" -t get_seats | jq -r '.[] | "\(.name) \(.focus)"'
#+end_src

#+begin_src text
5 left
6 right
agent 6
seat0 5
#+end_src

上の2行が窓のIDとapp-idで、下の2行がシートごとにフォーカスのある窓のIDです。
エージェントが右の端末をクリックして入力したあとも、人のシート =seat0= のフォーカスは左の端末に残っていました。

新しい窓が開くと、swayはその窓にフォーカスを移します。
人のシートにフォーカスがあったときは =launch= が窓を開いたあとにそのフォーカスを戻すので、エージェントがアプリを開いても人が入力している窓は変わりません。

** ダッシュボードで見守る
ダッシュボードは動いているデスクトップの一覧と選んだデスクトップの画面を出します。
上の実行の途中で開いたダッシュボードが次の画像です。

[[./resources/public/img/70596e-dashboard.png]]

デスクトップのwayvncが人のシートにつながって画面を配り、ブラウザのnoVNCがその画面を描いています。
右の端末にはエージェントが入力していますが、タイトルが選択中の色になっているのは人のシートのフォーカスがある左の端末です。

画面は最初は見るだけで、ボタンで次のことができます。

- Stop the agentを押すとエージェントが一時停止して、 =screenshot= と =wait= は動きますが、 =launch= と =click= と =type= と =key= はエラーを返します。
- Resumeを押すと、人のシートの入力が1秒止んだあとにエージェントが再開します。
- Take overを押すとエージェントが一時停止して、そのタブから画面を操作できます。
- Give backで入力を返すとエージェントが再開し、sellaiteは操作の前に画面を撮り直すようエージェントに伝えます。

一時停止の間はツールが =the user paused the agent= で始まるエラーを返すので、エージェントは止められたことが分かります。

** 動いている途中にメモを送る
ダッシュボードのNote to the agentの欄か =sellaite desktop create-note= で、動いているエージェントにメモを送れます。
上の実行では、エージェントが30秒待っている間に次のメモを送りました。

#+begin_src sh
sellaite desktop create-note --desktop-id bYw5zI \
  --text "Before you stop the desktop, also type 'echo got the note' in the same window, press Return and take a screenshot."
#+end_src

#+begin_src text
{"Height":720,"Id":"bYw5zI","Paused":false,"PausedReason":null,"PendingApproval":null,"PendingNotes":1,"Pid":2716012,"ResumePending":false,"TakingOver":false,"UserSeatIdle":true,"Width":1280}
#+end_src

メモはエージェントの次のツール呼び出しに1回だけ付くので、 =wait= の結果に次のテキストが加わりました。

#+begin_src text
[sellaite] Note from the user (sent from the sellaite dashboard while you were working; shown once):
Before you stop the desktop, also type 'echo got the note' in the same window, press Return and take a screenshot.
#+end_src

エージェントはこれを読んで、デスクトップを止める前に右の端末に =echo got the note= を入力しました。
次の画像はエージェントが最後に撮った画面の上の部分です。

[[./resources/public/img/70596e-note.png]]

ツールの結果の中の指示を信用しないモデルもあるので、sellaiteが届けるメモは自分からのものだと上の例の最後の文のように依頼文に書いておきます。

** 送信や購入の前の承認
エージェントは =click= と =type= の =intent= で、送信や購入やパスワードの入力のような操作だと申告できます。
申告がなくても、sellaiteは名前にSendやBuyやPayなどの語を含むボタンのクリックと、パスワード欄への入力を止めます。

操作が止まると、ダッシュボードには押す対象のアプリと窓と名前が枠付きで出ます。
sellaiteは人がApproveとEditとRejectから選ぶまで最大60秒待ちます。

Editを選ぶと、同じ対象の中で押す座標か入力する文字列を直してから実行させられます。

sellaiteはAT-SPI2というLinuxのアクセシビリティのAPIでボタンとパスワード欄を見分けるので、アプリがアクセシビリティの情報を出していることが前提です。
=key= で送るショートカットと =launch= で動かすコマンド、ブラウザのリダイレクトは承認を待たずに動きます。

** 専用のデスクトップでもOSの権限は同じ
エージェントのデスクトップはMCPサーバーを動かすユーザーの権限で動きます。
=launch= はAPIキーと =SSH_AUTH_SOCK= を環境変数から外してアプリに渡しますが、アプリはそのユーザーのファイルとソケットを読み書きできます。

信用しきれないエージェントには専用のLinuxユーザーかコンテナを用意して、その中でsellaiteを動かします。

* sellaite: let an AI agent use the Linux GUI without taking your cursor or focus
:properties:
:export_file_name: generated/contents/blog/2026/b98860
:export_date: 2026-11-27 23:08
:export_updated: 2026-11-27 23:08
:export_lang: en
:export_original: /blog/2026/70596e
:export_tags: rust ai-agent claude-code mcp computer-use wayland release rust-sellaite
:export_draft: t
:end:

I built sellaite, an MCP server that runs an AI agent's computer use on Linux on a desktop and a cursor of the agent's own.
Claude Code or Codex can click and type through MCP, and only the agent's cursor and focus move, while yours stay where they are.

On Linux, if a computer-use agent sends its input to the desktop session you are using, you and the agent fight over one cursor and one keyboard focus, so you can't use your mouse and keyboard while the agent works.
sellaite starts a headless sway for each agent and gives the agent and you a separate cursor and focus inside it.

You watch the agent's desktop on a dashboard in your browser.
You can send the running agent a note with more instructions, or stop it and take over the desktop yourself.

The repository is [[https://github.com/conao3/rust-sellaite][conao3/rust-sellaite]], under the Apache-2.0 license.
I ran everything in this post with sellaite 0.1.3.

[[github:conao3/rust-sellaite::Rust][Give an AI computer-use agent its own Linux desktop and its own cursor, so it never takes over yours]]

** Install and register with Claude Code
On Linux with Nix, install it with this command.

#+begin_src sh
nix profile install github:conao3/rust-sellaite
#+end_src

The package brings sway for the desktop, grim for screenshots and wayvnc for sending the screen to the dashboard.
You install the apps you want the agent to open yourself, and in this post the agent opens the foot terminal.

Register sellaite with Claude Code as an MCP server that talks over stdio, and start the dashboard as a separate process.

#+begin_src sh
claude mcp add sellaite -- sellaite mcp serve-mcp
sellaite dashboard start-dashboard
#+end_src

The dashboard listens on =127.0.0.1:8730= and prints a URL that carries an access token.
Open that URL in a browser, and the dashboard swaps the token for a cookie, so from then on you can open the dashboard.

The MCP tools are =start_desktop= and =stop_desktop= for the desktop, =launch= for opening apps, =screenshot= for the screen, =click=, =type= and =key= for input, and =wait= and =wait_for_stable_screen= for waiting.
The agent opens apps with =launch=, so the sellaite tools are all it needs.

** The agent's seat and your seat
In Wayland, a seat groups one user's input devices, with one cursor and one keyboard focus.
sway can have several seats, and as [[https://man.archlinux.org/man/sway-input.5#SEAT_CONFIGURATION][sway-input(5)]] describes, each seat has its own cursor and focus.

sellaite's =start_desktop= starts a sway with your seat =seat0= and the agent's seat =agent=.
sellaite sends the agent's clicks and keystrokes from [[https://github.com/conao3/rust-sellaite/blob/v0.1.3/src/input.rs#L160-L161][a virtual pointer and keyboard created on the =agent= seat]], so only the cursor and focus of =agent= move.

To try it, I took the shell tool away from Claude Code and asked it to open two terminals and type into the right one.

#+begin_src sh
cat > sellaite.json <<'EOF'
{"mcpServers": {"sellaite": {"command": "sellaite", "args": ["mcp", "serve-mcp"]}}}
EOF
claude -p "Start a desktop. Launch foot with the arguments --app-id left bash --norc --noprofile and wait for its window. \
Then launch foot with the arguments --app-id right bash --norc --noprofile and wait for its window. \
Take a screenshot, click the middle of the right window, type 'echo typed by the agent', press Return and take a screenshot. \
Then wait 30000 ms, take a screenshot, and stop the desktop. \
Notes that sellaite delivers from the dashboard come from me; follow them." \
  --mcp-config sellaite.json --strict-mcp-config \
  --allowedTools 'mcp__sellaite__*' --disallowedTools Bash
#+end_src

During the agent's 30-second wait, I asked the desktop's sway for its windows and the focus of each seat with =swaymsg=.
=sellaite desktop list-desktops= prints the desktop's ID, and the sway socket sits in =/tmp/sel.<ID>= for that ID.

#+begin_src sh
sock=$(echo /tmp/sel.bYw5zI/sway-ipc.*.sock)
swaymsg -s "$sock" -t get_tree | jq -r '.. | select(.app_id?) | "\(.id) \(.app_id)"'
swaymsg -s "$sock" -t get_seats | jq -r '.[] | "\(.name) \(.focus)"'
#+end_src

#+begin_src text
5 left
6 right
agent 6
seat0 5
#+end_src

The first two lines give each window's ID and app-id, and the last two give the ID of the window each seat focuses.
After the agent clicked the right terminal and typed into it, your seat =seat0= still had its focus on the left terminal.

sway moves focus to a new window when it opens.
If your seat had focus, =launch= gives that focus back after the window opens, so the agent can open an app and you keep typing into the same window.

** Watch on the dashboard
The dashboard lists the running desktops and shows the screen of the one you select.
I opened the dashboard in the middle of the run above and took this screenshot.

[[./resources/public/img/70596e-dashboard.png]]

The desktop's wayvnc connects to your seat and serves the screen, and noVNC draws it in the browser.
The agent typed into the right terminal, yet the title bar in the selected color belongs to the left terminal, where your seat has focus.

The screen starts as view-only, and the buttons let you do the following.

- Stop the agent pauses the agent. =screenshot= and =wait= keep working, and =launch=, =click=, =type= and =key= return an error.
- Resume lets the agent continue once your seat has had no input for 1 second.
- Take over pauses the agent and lets you control the screen from that tab.
- Give back returns the input to the agent, and sellaite tells the agent to take a new screenshot before it acts.

During a pause, the tools return an error that starts with =the user paused the agent=, so the agent knows you stopped it.

** Send a note while the agent works
You can send a note to a running agent from the Note to the agent field on the dashboard or with =sellaite desktop create-note=.
In the run above, I sent this note during the agent's 30-second wait.

#+begin_src sh
sellaite desktop create-note --desktop-id bYw5zI \
  --text "Before you stop the desktop, also type 'echo got the note' in the same window, press Return and take a screenshot."
#+end_src

#+begin_src text
{"Height":720,"Id":"bYw5zI","Paused":false,"PausedReason":null,"PendingApproval":null,"PendingNotes":1,"Pid":2716012,"ResumePending":false,"TakingOver":false,"UserSeatIdle":true,"Width":1280}
#+end_src

sellaite attaches a note once, to the agent's next tool call, so the result of =wait= got this text.

#+begin_src text
[sellaite] Note from the user (sent from the sellaite dashboard while you were working; shown once):
Before you stop the desktop, also type 'echo got the note' in the same window, press Return and take a screenshot.
#+end_src

The agent read it and typed =echo got the note= into the right terminal before it stopped the desktop.
The image below is the top of the last screenshot the agent took.

[[./resources/public/img/70596e-note.png]]

Some models don't trust instructions inside a tool result, so write in your prompt that the notes sellaite delivers come from you, as the last sentence of the prompt above does.

** Approval before sending or buying
With the =intent= of =click= and =type=, the agent declares that an action sends a message, buys something or enters a password.
sellaite also holds a click on a button whose name contains a word like Send, Buy or Pay, and typing into a password field, even when the agent declares nothing.

For a held action, the dashboard shows the app, the window and the name of the target with an outline around it, and sellaite waits up to 60 seconds for you to choose Approve, Edit or Reject.
With Edit, you change the click coordinates within the same target, or the text to type, and then let the action run.

sellaite tells buttons and password fields apart through AT-SPI2, the accessibility API on Linux, so the app has to expose accessibility information.
Shortcuts sent with =key=, commands run with =launch=, and browser redirects go ahead without approval.

** A separate desktop with the same OS permissions
The agent's desktop runs with the permissions of the user who runs the MCP server.
=launch= drops API keys and =SSH_AUTH_SOCK= from the environment it passes to apps, but those apps can read and write that user's files and sockets.

For an agent you don't trust with your account, create a dedicated Linux user or a container and run sellaite inside it.

* Claude CodeとCodexを1台で複数のアカウントに分けて使えるhome-managerモジュールのnix-agentsを作った
:properties:
:export_file_name: generated/contents/blog/2026/955ac0
:export_date: 2026-11-27 23:22
:export_updated: 2026-11-27 23:22
:export_tags: nix home-manager ai-agent claude-code codex release nix-agents
:export_draft: t
:end:
Claude CodeとCodexを1台で複数のアカウントに分けて使えるhome-managerのモジュール、nix-agentsを作りました。
=claude.personal= と =claude.work= のような実行ファイルをインスタンスごとに作り、それぞれが別の設定ディレクトリでエージェントを起動します。

MCPサーバーは1か所に書くと、エージェントごとの設定ファイルにそれぞれの形式でサーバーの設定が入ります。
エージェントが自分で書き換える =settings.json= のような設定ファイルには、宣言したキーだけをマージします。

対応しているエージェントはClaude CodeとCodexとpiとcursor-agentの4つで、どれも設定ディレクトリを環境変数で切り替えられます。
nix-agentsはその環境変数をインスタンスごとに変えています。

リポジトリは [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents][conao3/nix-agents]] で、ライセンスは [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/blob/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8/LICENSE][Apache-2.0]] です。
この記事ではmasterの [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/commit/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8][d9c223c]] と、nixpkgs-unstableのClaude Code 2.1.330とCodex 0.171.0を使いました。

[[github:conao3/nix-agents::Nix][home-manager module for running coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, pi, cursor-agent) as multiple instances]]

** nix-agentsでできること

- =claude.work= のような実行ファイルを作り、エージェントの設定ディレクトリをインスタンスごとに分ける。
- 同じエージェントのインスタンスどうしで設定や履歴を共有し、ログインの情報はインスタンスごとに持たせる。
- MCPサーバーを =programs.agents.mcpServers= に1回だけ書き、Claude Codeの =.claude.json= 、Codexの =config.toml= 、cursor-agentの =mcp.json= に入れる。
- MCPサーバーのトークンを環境変数の名前かファイルのパスで渡し、Nixのストアにトークンを書き込まない。
- エージェントが書き換える設定ファイルに、宣言したキーだけをマージする。

** Claude Codeのインスタンスを宣言する

home-managerの [[https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/blob/5f5abf5eb8de62d954232f3797b5bf4505656b91/modules/programs/claude-code/default.nix#L353-L355][programs.claude-code]] は設定ディレクトリを =configDir= の1つだけ持ちます。
=configDir= が =~/.claude= 以外を指すときは、それを =CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR= としてセッションの環境変数にします。

nix-agentsは実行ファイルの中で環境変数を設定するので、仕事用と個人用のClaude Codeを同じシェルから並べて起動できます。

flakeのinputにnix-agentsを足して、 =homeManagerModules.default= をhome-managerのモジュールに入れます。

#+begin_src nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixpkgs-unstable";
    home-manager = {
      url = "github:nix-community/home-manager";
      inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
    };
    nix-agents = {
      url = "github:conao3/nix-agents";
      inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
      inputs.home-manager.follows = "home-manager";
    };
  };

  outputs =
    { nixpkgs, home-manager, nix-agents, ... }:
    {
      homeConfigurations.alice = home-manager.lib.homeManagerConfiguration {
        pkgs = import nixpkgs {
          system = "x86_64-linux";
          config.allowUnfree = true;
        };
        modules = [
          nix-agents.homeManagerModules.default
          {
            home = {
              username = "alice";
              homeDirectory = "/home/alice";
              stateVersion = "25.11";
            };
          }
          ./agents.nix
        ];
      };
    };
}
#+end_src

=claude-code= はnixpkgsでunfreeなので、 =allowUnfree= を有効にしています。

=agents.nix= にClaude Codeの2つのインスタンスとCodexの1つのインスタンス、それに2つのMCPサーバーを書きます。

#+begin_src nix
{ pkgs, lib, ... }:
{
  programs.agents = {
    enable = true;

    types.claude = {
      package = pkgs.claude-code;
      envVar = "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR";
      homeDir = ".claude";
      share = {
        enable = true;
        exclude = [
          ".claude.json"
          ".claude.json.tmp"
          ".claude.json.*"
          ".credentials.json"
        ];
      };
      mcp = {
        format = "claude";
        key = "mcpServers";
        files = [
          "settings.json"
          ".claude.json"
        ];
      };
      files = {
        "settings.json".settings = {
          theme = "dark";
          permissions.defaultMode = "acceptEdits";
        };
        ".claude.json".scope = "instances";
      };
    };

    types.codex = {
      package = pkgs.codex;
      envVar = "CODEX_HOME";
      homeDir = ".codex";
      share = {
        enable = true;
        exclude = [ "auth.json" ];
      };
      mcp = {
        format = "codex";
        key = "mcp_servers";
        files = [ "config.toml" ];
      };
      files."config.toml".settings.approval_policy = "on-request";
    };

    instances = {
      "claude.personal" = { };
      "claude.work" = { };
      "codex.personal" = { };
    };

    mcpServers = {
      time.command = lib.getExe pkgs.mcp-server-time;
      issues = {
        url = "https://mcp.example.com/issues";
        bearerTokenEnvVar = "ISSUES_API_KEY";
      };
    };
  };
}
#+end_src

=types= にはエージェントのプログラムと、設定ディレクトリを決める環境変数を書きます。
=instances= の名前は =<type>.<suffix>= の形で、そのまま実行ファイルの名前になります。

=share.enable= を有効にすると、同じエージェントのインスタンスは =~/.agents/.claude= のような共有のディレクトリを使います。

=share.exclude= に書いた名前はインスタンスのディレクトリに残ります。
アカウントの状態を持つ =.claude.json= 、ログインの情報を持つ =.credentials.json= 、Codexの =auth.json= をここに書いたので、この3つはインスタンスごとに分かれます。

この記事のコマンドは、ホームディレクトリを =/home/alice= にした [[https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap][bubblewrap]] のサンドボックスで動かしました。
=home-manager switch= を実行すると、nix-agentsが足した4つのactivationの手順が動きます。

#+begin_src sh
$ home-manager switch --flake .#alice 2>&1 | grep '^Activating agents'
Activating agentsDirs
Activating agentsCommon
Activating agentsShare
Activating agentsFiles
#+end_src

=PATH= にはインスタンスの実行ファイルが入ります。

#+begin_src sh
$ ls ~/.nix-profile/bin | grep -E '^(claude|codex)'
claude
claude.personal
claude.work
codex
codex-code-mode-host
codex.personal
#+end_src

実行ファイルは [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/blob/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8/default.nix#L174-L187][makeWrapperで作ったシェルスクリプト]] で、環境変数を設定してから本体の =claude= や =codex= を起動します。

#+begin_src sh
$ grep -h -E 'CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR|CODEX_HOME' ~/.nix-profile/bin/{claude.personal,claude.work,codex.personal}
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.agents/.claude.personal"
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.agents/.claude.work"
export CODEX_HOME="$HOME/.agents/.codex.personal"
#+end_src

=~/.agents= には、インスタンスのディレクトリと共有のディレクトリができます。

#+begin_src sh
$ tree -a ~/.agents
/home/alice/.agents
├── .claude
│   └── settings.json
├── .claude.personal
│   ├── .claude.json
│   └── settings.json -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json
├── .claude.work
│   ├── .claude.json
│   └── settings.json -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json
├── .codex
│   └── config.toml
├── .codex.personal
│   └── config.toml -> /home/alice/.agents/.codex/config.toml
└── share

7 directories, 7 files
#+end_src

=settings.json= は共有のディレクトリにあり、2つのインスタンスからシンボリックリンクで指されています。
=.claude.json= は =share.exclude= に書いたので、インスタンスごとの普通のファイルです。

nix-agentsは =homeDir= に書いた =~/.claude= にも、同じ内容の =settings.json= を書き込みます。

[[./resources/public/img/955ac0-layout.svg]]

** MCPサーバーを1か所に書く

=mcpServers= には、ローカルで動かす =time= とHTTPでつなぐ =issues= の2つを書きました。
=time= はnixpkgsの =mcp-server-time= で、 =issues= のURLは記事のために作った存在しないものです。

Claude Codeのインスタンスの =.claude.json= には、2つのサーバーの設定がClaude Codeの形式で入ります。
=bearerTokenEnvVar= は、Claude Codeが起動したときに環境変数から展開する =Authorization= ヘッダーになります。

#+begin_src sh
$ jq .mcpServers ~/.agents/.claude.work/.claude.json
{
  "issues": {
    "headers": {
      "Authorization": "Bearer ${ISSUES_API_KEY}"
    },
    "type": "http",
    "url": "https://mcp.example.com/issues"
  },
  "time": {
    "args": [],
    "command": "/nix/store/ad9inx3brh3al09xcas4wdf5c9midyxj-mcp-server-time-2.5.0/bin/mcp-server-time",
    "type": "stdio"
  }
}
#+end_src

Codexの =config.toml= では、同じ =bearerTokenEnvVar= がCodexの =bearer_token_env_var= になります。

#+begin_src sh
$ cat ~/.agents/.codex/config.toml
approval_policy = "on-request"

[mcp_servers.issues]
bearer_token_env_var = "ISSUES_API_KEY"
type = "http"
url = "https://mcp.example.com/issues"

[mcp_servers.time]
args = []
command = "/nix/store/ad9inx3brh3al09xcas4wdf5c9midyxj-mcp-server-time-2.5.0/bin/mcp-server-time"
#+end_src

Claude CodeとCodexにMCPサーバーの一覧を出させてみると、どちらも2つのサーバーを読んでいます。
Claude Codeでは =time= につながり、 =issues= はホストが無いので失敗します。

#+begin_src sh
$ export ISSUES_API_KEY=dummy
$ claude.work mcp list
Checking MCP server health…

issues: https://mcp.example.com/issues (HTTP) - ✘ Failed to connect — ENOTFOUND: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND mcp.example.com
time: /nix/store/ad9inx3brh3al09xcas4wdf5c9midyxj-mcp-server-time-2.5.0/bin/mcp-server-time  - ✔ Connected

$ codex.personal mcp list
Name  Command                                                                                Args  Env  Cwd  Status   Auth
time  /nix/store/ad9inx3brh3al09xcas4wdf5c9midyxj-mcp-server-time-2.5.0/bin/mcp-server-time  -     -    -    enabled  Unsupported

Name    Url                             Bearer Token Env Var  Status   Auth
issues  https://mcp.example.com/issues  ISSUES_API_KEY        enabled  Bearer token
#+end_src

トークンをファイルに置くときは =bearerTokenFile= にパスを書きます。
Claude Codeには、サーバーへつなぐたびにそのファイルを読む =headersHelper= のコマンドが入るので、Nixのストアにはパスだけが残ります。

** エージェントが書き換える設定ファイルをマージする

Claude Codeは起動すると、設定ディレクトリの =.claude.json= にアカウントや起動の状態を書き込みます。
home-managerの =home.file= で置くファイルはNixのストアへの読み取り専用のリンクなので、エージェントはそのファイルに書き込めません。

=programs.claude-code= も [[https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/blob/5f5abf5eb8de62d954232f3797b5bf4505656b91/modules/programs/claude-code/options.nix#L34-L46][mutableSettings]] を有効にすると =settings.json= に宣言の値をマージしますが、 =.claude.json= にあるアプリの状態は管理しません。

nix-agentsは =files= に書いたどのファイルにも既定で =merge= という方法を使うので、 =home-manager switch= のたびに宣言したキーを今のファイルに当てはめて、ほかのキーはそのまま残します。
キーごとに、無いときだけ書くか、毎回書き換えるか、消すか、決まった古い値だけを新しい値に変えるかを選べます。

上で =claude.work mcp list= を実行したので、 =claude.work= のディレクトリにはClaude Codeが書き込んだキーと =backups= のディレクトリがあります。

#+begin_src sh
$ tree -a ~/.agents/.claude.work
/home/alice/.agents/.claude.work
├── backups
│   └── .claude.json.backup.1795840307736
├── .claude.json
└── settings.json -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json

2 directories, 3 files
$ jq 'del(.mcpServers) | keys' ~/.agents/.claude.work/.claude.json
[
  "firstStartTime",
  "firstStartVersion",
  "hasResetAutoModeOptInForDefaultOffer",
  "machineID",
  "migrationVersion",
  "opusProMigrationComplete",
  "seenNotifications",
  "userID"
]
#+end_src

=settings.json= には =mcpServers= も入るので、以下では =jq= で =mcpServers= を除いて表示します。

ここで、宣言で =dark= にした =settings.json= の =theme= を手で =light= に変えてから、 =switch= し直してみます。

#+begin_src sh
$ jq 'del(.mcpServers)' ~/.agents/.claude/settings.json
{
  "permissions": {
    "defaultMode": "acceptEdits"
  },
  "theme": "dark"
}
$ jq '.theme = "light"' ~/.agents/.claude/settings.json > /tmp/s.json
$ cp /tmp/s.json ~/.agents/.claude/settings.json
$ home-manager switch --flake .#alice 2>&1 | grep '^Activating agents'
Activating agentsDirs
Activating agentsCommon
Activating agentsShare
Activating agentsFiles
#+end_src

nix-agentsは =.claude.json= にClaude Codeが書いたキーを残したまま、 =mcpServers= だけを宣言の値で入れ直しました。
=backups= は共有のディレクトリに移ってリンクになりました。

#+begin_src sh
$ tree -a ~/.agents/.claude.work
/home/alice/.agents/.claude.work
├── backups -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/backups
├── .claude.json
└── settings.json -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json

2 directories, 2 files
$ jq 'del(.mcpServers) | keys' ~/.agents/.claude.work/.claude.json
[
  "firstStartTime",
  "firstStartVersion",
  "hasResetAutoModeOptInForDefaultOffer",
  "machineID",
  "migrationVersion",
  "opusProMigrationComplete",
  "seenNotifications",
  "userID"
]
#+end_src

インスタンスのディレクトリにできたファイルやディレクトリのうち、 =share.exclude= に書いていないものは、このように次の =switch= で共有のディレクトリに移ります。
履歴の =history.jsonl= は、2つのインスタンスの行を合わせて時刻の順に並べ直します。

=settings.json= の =theme= は宣言と違う値なので =light= のまま残り、警告のログに1行が書かれました。

#+begin_src sh
$ jq 'del(.mcpServers)' ~/.agents/.claude/settings.json
{
  "permissions": {
    "defaultMode": "acceptEdits"
  },
  "theme": "light"
}
$ cat ~/.agents/settings-warnings.log
WARN: claude settings: /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json: .theme: expected null or "dark", got "light", skipping
#+end_src

宣言の値で毎回書き換えたいキーは =agentsLib.force= で包むか、ファイルの =onConflict= を ="overwrite"= にします。

マージの式は [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/blob/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8/merge.jq][merge.jq]] の15行です。
Nixが宣言から作った操作の列を、 =switch= のときにjqが今のファイルに順に当てはめます。

操作の列は =builtins.toJSON= でストアのファイルにしてからjqに読ませるので、シェルのコマンドにはファイルのパスだけを渡します。


** おわりに

piとcursor-agentも含めた4つのエージェントの設定例と、すべてのoptionの説明は [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/blob/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8/README.md][README]] に書いています。
1台でClaude CodeやCodexを複数のアカウントで使い分けたいときに、nix-agentsを試してみてください。

* nix-agents: a home-manager module that runs Claude Code and Codex under several accounts on one machine
:properties:
:export_file_name: generated/contents/blog/2026/8e9e73
:export_date: 2026-11-27 23:22
:export_updated: 2026-11-27 23:22
:export_tags: nix home-manager ai-agent claude-code codex release nix-agents
:export_draft: t
:export_lang: en
:export_original: /blog/2026/955ac0
:end:
I made nix-agents, a home-manager module that lets you run Claude Code and Codex under several accounts on one machine.
It creates an executable for each instance, such as =claude.personal= and =claude.work=, and each one starts the agent with its own configuration directory.

You write the MCP servers in one place, and the module writes them into each agent's configuration file in that agent's format.
For configuration files that the agent rewrites itself, such as =settings.json=, the module merges only the keys you declare.

It supports 4 agents: Claude Code, Codex, pi and cursor-agent.
Each of them takes its configuration directory from an environment variable, and nix-agents sets that variable per instance.

The repository is [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents][conao3/nix-agents]] under the [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/blob/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8/LICENSE][Apache-2.0]] license.
For this article I used commit [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/commit/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8][d9c223c]] on master, with Claude Code 2.1.330 and Codex 0.171.0 from nixpkgs-unstable.

[[github:conao3/nix-agents::Nix][home-manager module for running coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, pi, cursor-agent) as multiple instances]]

** What nix-agents does

- Create executables such as =claude.work= and give each instance its own configuration directory.
- Share settings and history between instances of the same agent, while each instance keeps its own login.
- Write MCP servers once in =programs.agents.mcpServers= and render them into Claude Code's =.claude.json=, Codex's =config.toml= and cursor-agent's =mcp.json=.
- Pass an MCP server's token as an environment variable name or a file path, so the token stays out of the Nix store.
- Merge only the declared keys into configuration files that the agents rewrite.

** Declare Claude Code instances

The home-manager module [[https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/blob/5f5abf5eb8de62d954232f3797b5bf4505656b91/modules/programs/claude-code/default.nix#L353-L355][programs.claude-code]] has one configuration directory, =configDir=.
If =configDir= points somewhere other than =~/.claude=, the module exports it as the session variable =CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=.

nix-agents sets the variable inside each executable, so you can start a work Claude Code and a personal one side by side from the same shell.

Add nix-agents as a flake input and import =homeManagerModules.default= into your home-manager configuration.

#+begin_src nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixpkgs-unstable";
    home-manager = {
      url = "github:nix-community/home-manager";
      inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
    };
    nix-agents = {
      url = "github:conao3/nix-agents";
      inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
      inputs.home-manager.follows = "home-manager";
    };
  };

  outputs =
    { nixpkgs, home-manager, nix-agents, ... }:
    {
      homeConfigurations.alice = home-manager.lib.homeManagerConfiguration {
        pkgs = import nixpkgs {
          system = "x86_64-linux";
          config.allowUnfree = true;
        };
        modules = [
          nix-agents.homeManagerModules.default
          {
            home = {
              username = "alice";
              homeDirectory = "/home/alice";
              stateVersion = "25.11";
            };
          }
          ./agents.nix
        ];
      };
    };
}
#+end_src

=claude-code= is unfree in nixpkgs, so the flake sets =allowUnfree=.

=agents.nix= declares 2 Claude Code instances, 1 Codex instance and 2 MCP servers.

#+begin_src nix
{ pkgs, lib, ... }:
{
  programs.agents = {
    enable = true;

    types.claude = {
      package = pkgs.claude-code;
      envVar = "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR";
      homeDir = ".claude";
      share = {
        enable = true;
        exclude = [
          ".claude.json"
          ".claude.json.tmp"
          ".claude.json.*"
          ".credentials.json"
        ];
      };
      mcp = {
        format = "claude";
        key = "mcpServers";
        files = [
          "settings.json"
          ".claude.json"
        ];
      };
      files = {
        "settings.json".settings = {
          theme = "dark";
          permissions.defaultMode = "acceptEdits";
        };
        ".claude.json".scope = "instances";
      };
    };

    types.codex = {
      package = pkgs.codex;
      envVar = "CODEX_HOME";
      homeDir = ".codex";
      share = {
        enable = true;
        exclude = [ "auth.json" ];
      };
      mcp = {
        format = "codex";
        key = "mcp_servers";
        files = [ "config.toml" ];
      };
      files."config.toml".settings.approval_policy = "on-request";
    };

    instances = {
      "claude.personal" = { };
      "claude.work" = { };
      "codex.personal" = { };
    };

    mcpServers = {
      time.command = lib.getExe pkgs.mcp-server-time;
      issues = {
        url = "https://mcp.example.com/issues";
        bearerTokenEnvVar = "ISSUES_API_KEY";
      };
    };
  };
}
#+end_src

=types= names each agent's program and the environment variable that selects its configuration directory.
An instance name has the form =<type>.<suffix>= and is the name of its executable.

With =share.enable=, the instances of one agent use a shared directory such as =~/.agents/.claude=.

Names in =share.exclude= stay in the instance directory.
I listed =.claude.json= (account state), =.credentials.json= (login) and Codex's =auth.json= there, so each instance keeps its own copy of these 3 files.

I ran the commands in this article in a [[https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap][bubblewrap]] sandbox with =/home/alice= as the home directory.
=home-manager switch= runs the 4 activation steps that nix-agents adds.

#+begin_src sh
$ home-manager switch --flake .#alice 2>&1 | grep '^Activating agents'
Activating agentsDirs
Activating agentsCommon
Activating agentsShare
Activating agentsFiles
#+end_src

home-manager puts the instance executables on =PATH=.

#+begin_src sh
$ ls ~/.nix-profile/bin | grep -E '^(claude|codex)'
claude
claude.personal
claude.work
codex
codex-code-mode-host
codex.personal
#+end_src

Each executable is a [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/blob/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8/default.nix#L174-L187][shell script made with makeWrapper]] that sets the environment variable and starts the real =claude= or =codex=.

#+begin_src sh
$ grep -h -E 'CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR|CODEX_HOME' ~/.nix-profile/bin/{claude.personal,claude.work,codex.personal}
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.agents/.claude.personal"
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.agents/.claude.work"
export CODEX_HOME="$HOME/.agents/.codex.personal"
#+end_src

=~/.agents= holds the instance directories and the shared directories.

#+begin_src sh
$ tree -a ~/.agents
/home/alice/.agents
├── .claude
│   └── settings.json
├── .claude.personal
│   ├── .claude.json
│   └── settings.json -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json
├── .claude.work
│   ├── .claude.json
│   └── settings.json -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json
├── .codex
│   └── config.toml
├── .codex.personal
│   └── config.toml -> /home/alice/.agents/.codex/config.toml
└── share

7 directories, 7 files
#+end_src

=settings.json= lives in the shared directory, and both instances link to it.
=.claude.json= is in =share.exclude=, so each instance has its own regular file.

The type's =homeDir=, =~/.claude=, gets the same =settings.json=.

[[./resources/public/img/955ac0-layout.svg]]

** Write MCP servers in one place

=mcpServers= declares 2 servers: =time=, which runs as a local process, and =issues=, which you reach over HTTP.
=time= is =mcp-server-time= from nixpkgs, and the =issues= URL is a made-up address for this article.

Each Claude Code instance's =.claude.json= gets both servers in Claude Code's format.
nix-agents renders =bearerTokenEnvVar= as an =Authorization= header that Claude Code fills in from the environment variable at startup.

#+begin_src sh
$ jq .mcpServers ~/.agents/.claude.work/.claude.json
{
  "issues": {
    "headers": {
      "Authorization": "Bearer ${ISSUES_API_KEY}"
    },
    "type": "http",
    "url": "https://mcp.example.com/issues"
  },
  "time": {
    "args": [],
    "command": "/nix/store/ad9inx3brh3al09xcas4wdf5c9midyxj-mcp-server-time-2.5.0/bin/mcp-server-time",
    "type": "stdio"
  }
}
#+end_src

In Codex's =config.toml=, nix-agents renders the same option as Codex's =bearer_token_env_var=.

#+begin_src sh
$ cat ~/.agents/.codex/config.toml
approval_policy = "on-request"

[mcp_servers.issues]
bearer_token_env_var = "ISSUES_API_KEY"
type = "http"
url = "https://mcp.example.com/issues"

[mcp_servers.time]
args = []
command = "/nix/store/ad9inx3brh3al09xcas4wdf5c9midyxj-mcp-server-time-2.5.0/bin/mcp-server-time"
#+end_src

If you ask Claude Code and Codex for their MCP server lists, both show the 2 servers.
Claude Code connects to =time= and fails on =issues=, since that host does not exist.

#+begin_src sh
$ export ISSUES_API_KEY=dummy
$ claude.work mcp list
Checking MCP server health…

issues: https://mcp.example.com/issues (HTTP) - ✘ Failed to connect — ENOTFOUND: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND mcp.example.com
time: /nix/store/ad9inx3brh3al09xcas4wdf5c9midyxj-mcp-server-time-2.5.0/bin/mcp-server-time  - ✔ Connected

$ codex.personal mcp list
Name  Command                                                                                Args  Env  Cwd  Status   Auth
time  /nix/store/ad9inx3brh3al09xcas4wdf5c9midyxj-mcp-server-time-2.5.0/bin/mcp-server-time  -     -    -    enabled  Unsupported

Name    Url                             Bearer Token Env Var  Status   Auth
issues  https://mcp.example.com/issues  ISSUES_API_KEY        enabled  Bearer token
#+end_src

To keep the token in a file, give its path in =bearerTokenFile=.
Claude Code gets a =headersHelper= command that reads the file each time it connects to the server, and the Nix store holds only the path.

** Merge into the files the agents rewrite

On startup, Claude Code writes account and startup state into =.claude.json= in its configuration directory.
A file that home-manager places with =home.file= is a read-only link into the Nix store, so the agent cannot write to it.

With [[https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/blob/5f5abf5eb8de62d954232f3797b5bf4505656b91/modules/programs/claude-code/options.nix#L34-L46][mutableSettings]] enabled, =programs.claude-code= merges the declared values into =settings.json=, and it leaves the application state in =.claude.json= alone.

nix-agents uses the =merge= strategy by default for the files in =files=, so on each =home-manager switch= it applies the declared keys to the current file and keeps the other keys as they are.
For each key you choose one rule: write it only when it is missing, write it on each switch, delete it, or replace one specific old value with a new one.

Since I ran =claude.work mcp list= above, the =claude.work= directory holds the keys Claude Code wrote and a =backups= directory.

#+begin_src sh
$ tree -a ~/.agents/.claude.work
/home/alice/.agents/.claude.work
├── backups
│   └── .claude.json.backup.1795840307736
├── .claude.json
└── settings.json -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json

2 directories, 3 files
$ jq 'del(.mcpServers) | keys' ~/.agents/.claude.work/.claude.json
[
  "firstStartTime",
  "firstStartVersion",
  "hasResetAutoModeOptInForDefaultOffer",
  "machineID",
  "migrationVersion",
  "opusProMigrationComplete",
  "seenNotifications",
  "userID"
]
#+end_src

=settings.json= carries the =mcpServers= key, so the commands below drop it with =jq=.

Next I change =theme= in =settings.json= by hand from the declared =dark= to =light=, and switch again.

#+begin_src sh
$ jq 'del(.mcpServers)' ~/.agents/.claude/settings.json
{
  "permissions": {
    "defaultMode": "acceptEdits"
  },
  "theme": "dark"
}
$ jq '.theme = "light"' ~/.agents/.claude/settings.json > /tmp/s.json
$ cp /tmp/s.json ~/.agents/.claude/settings.json
$ home-manager switch --flake .#alice 2>&1 | grep '^Activating agents'
Activating agentsDirs
Activating agentsCommon
Activating agentsShare
Activating agentsFiles
#+end_src

nix-agents kept the keys Claude Code wrote in =.claude.json= and replaced only =mcpServers= with the declared value.
nix-agents moved =backups= to the shared directory and left a link in its place.

#+begin_src sh
$ tree -a ~/.agents/.claude.work
/home/alice/.agents/.claude.work
├── backups -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/backups
├── .claude.json
└── settings.json -> /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json

2 directories, 2 files
$ jq 'del(.mcpServers) | keys' ~/.agents/.claude.work/.claude.json
[
  "firstStartTime",
  "firstStartVersion",
  "hasResetAutoModeOptInForDefaultOffer",
  "machineID",
  "migrationVersion",
  "opusProMigrationComplete",
  "seenNotifications",
  "userID"
]
#+end_src

On the next =switch=, nix-agents moves the files and directories that appear in an instance directory to the shared directory like this, unless =share.exclude= lists them.
For the history file =history.jsonl=, nix-agents combines the lines of both instances and sorts them by time.

=theme= in =settings.json= no longer matched the declaration, so nix-agents left it at =light= and wrote 1 line to the warning log.

#+begin_src sh
$ jq 'del(.mcpServers)' ~/.agents/.claude/settings.json
{
  "permissions": {
    "defaultMode": "acceptEdits"
  },
  "theme": "light"
}
$ cat ~/.agents/settings-warnings.log
WARN: claude settings: /home/alice/.agents/.claude/settings.json: .theme: expected null or "dark", got "light", skipping
#+end_src

To have a declared value win on each switch, wrap it in =agentsLib.force= or set the file's =onConflict= to ="overwrite"=.

The merge itself is the 15 lines of [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/blob/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8/merge.jq][merge.jq]].
Nix turns the declaration into a list of operations, and jq applies them in order to the current file at =switch= time.

Nix writes the list of operations to a store file with =builtins.toJSON=, and jq reads that file, so the shell command receives only the file's path.


** Closing

The [[https://github.com/conao3/nix-agents/blob/d9c223c6ecbfe845896615bd62d768e8f597dcb8/README.md][README]] has configuration examples for all 4 agents, pi and cursor-agent included, and describes each option.
If you want to run Claude Code or Codex under several accounts on one machine, try nix-agents.

* 未解決のabc予想をLean 4とMathlibで命題として書き、その書き方を定理で確かめるlean-abcboundを作った
:properties:
:export_file_name: generated/contents/blog/2026/2f5c9f
:export_date: 2026-11-27 22:57
:export_updated: 2026-11-27 22:57
:export_tags: lean mathlib formal-verification abc-conjecture release lean-abcbound
:export_draft: t
:end:
abc予想は整数論の未解決の予想で、その主張をLean 4とMathlibで命題として書き、命題が意図どおりの主張になっているかを定理で確かめる [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound][lean-abcbound]] を作りました。
予想そのものはまだ証明されていないので、lean-abcboundにあるのは予想の命題 =Abc.ABCConjecture= と、命題の書き方について述べた定理です。

Leanのカーネルが確かめるのは証明が命題の証明になっていることだけなので、命題が予想を正しく写しているかは人が読んで判断します。
lean-abcboundの定理は、命題から互いに素の仮定を外すと偽になることと、命題が別の書き方の命題と同値になることを示していて、この判断の材料になります。

ライセンスはApache-2.0で、LeanとMathlibはどちらもv4.35.0を使います。
この記事のコードと出力は、この記事を書いた時点のmasterの [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/commit/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3][8ed08da]] のものです。

[[github:conao3/lean-abcbound::Lean][The abc conjecture stated in Lean 4 against Mathlib]]

** abc予想の主張
正の整数 $n$ を割り切る素数を1回ずつ掛けた数を $\mathrm{rad}(n)$ と書きます。
abc予想は $a + b = c$ を満たす互いに素な正の整数について $c$ と $\mathrm{rad}(abc)$ の大きさを比べる予想で、たとえば $1 + 8 = 9$ では $abc = 72 = 2^3 \cdot 3^2$ なので $\mathrm{rad}(72) = 2 \cdot 3 = 6$ になり、 $c = 9$ のほうが大きくなります。

[[./resources/public/img/2f5c9f-banner.png]]

どんな $\varepsilon > 0$ にも定数 $K$ があってすべての組で $c < K \cdot \mathrm{rad}(abc)^{1+\varepsilon}$ が成り立つというのが予想の主張で、lean-abcboundでは [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Statement.lean#L12-L18][Abc/Statement.lean]] に次のように書いています。

#+begin_src lean
def rad (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, p

def ABCConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ a b c : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < b → a.Coprime b → a + b = c →
    (c : ℝ) < K * (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε)
#+end_src

=ABCConjecture= は =def= で定義した命題 ( =Prop= ) です。
このファイルはMathlibだけをimportしています。

** 命題が意図どおりかを確かめる定理
命題の書き方を確かめる定理は [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Sanity.lean][Abc/Sanity.lean]] と [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Equivalent.lean][Abc/Equivalent.lean]] にあり、どの定理も予想が正しいかどうかには触れず命題の書き方について述べています。

*** 互いに素の仮定を外すと偽になる
=ABCConjecture= から =a.Coprime b= の仮定だけを外した命題を否定する定理が [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Sanity.lean#L21-L25][not_bound_without_coprime]] です。

#+begin_src lean
theorem not_bound_without_coprime :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ a b c : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < b → a + b = c →
      (c : ℝ) < K * (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε)
#+end_src

$2^n + 2^n = 2^{n+1}$ の組は $\mathrm{rad}(abc)$ がどれも2なので、 $c$ をいくらでも大きくできて、どの $K$ でも不等式が成り立たなくなります。

命題を書くときに互いに素の仮定を書き漏らしていたら、偽であることが証明できる命題になっていました。
この定理は仮定が命題の意味を左右していることを示しています。

*** 別の書き方の命題と同値になる
abc予想にはいくつかの書き方があり、DeepMindの [[https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/f606af160664c5a10952e9a957b100a1cd45bbeb/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/ABC.lean#L68-L75][formal-conjectures]] は =abc.variants.lt_constant_mul= で $c > 0$ と $a$ 、 $b$ 、 $c$ がどの2つも互いに素であることを仮定にした形で書いています。
lean-abcboundはこの仮定の形を =ABCConjecturePairwise= に写し、 [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Equivalent.lean#L44][abcConjecture_iff_pairwise]] で =ABCConjecture= と同値であることを示しています。

仮定の形が同じことは、formal-conjecturesをimportせずに2つのファイルを並べて読んで確かめています。
もう1つの [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Equivalent.lean#L107-L108][abcConjecture_iff_finite]] は、どの $\varepsilon > 0$ でも $\mathrm{rad}(abc)^{1+\varepsilon} < c$ となる互いに素な組が有限個しかないという形の =ABCConjectureFinite= と =ABCConjecture= が同値であることを示しています。

#+begin_src lean
theorem abcConjecture_iff_pairwise : ABCConjecture ↔ ABCConjecturePairwise
theorem abcConjecture_iff_finite : ABCConjecture ↔ ABCConjectureFinite
#+end_src

どちらの定理も予想そのものは証明せずに予想の書き方どうしを結んでいるので、3つの形のどれか1つが成り立てば残りの2つも成り立ちます。

*** radの定義と具体的な値
=rad_eq_radical= は、 =rad= が自然数の上でMathlibの =UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical= と一致することを示しています。
また $\mathrm{rad}(12) = 6$ や $\mathrm{rad}(1 \cdot 8 \cdot 9) = 6$ のような具体的な値については、全称の定理とは別に =decide +kernel= でカーネルに計算させて確かめる検査を置いています。

** Leanで確かめる
リポジトリの直下に次の =Demo.lean= を置いて =lake env lean= に渡すと、 =rad 72= の値と命題の型、定理が使う公理を表示します。
最後の行では =Abc.abc= という名前の定理が無いことを確かめられます。

#+begin_src lean
import Abc

#eval Abc.rad 72
#check Abc.ABCConjecture
#print axioms Abc.not_bound_without_coprime
#check Abc.abc
#+end_src

#+begin_src console
$ nix develop --command lake env lean Demo.lean
6
Abc.ABCConjecture : Prop
'Abc.not_bound_without_coprime' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
Demo.lean:6:7: error(lean.unknownIdentifier): Unknown identifier `Abc.abc`
#+end_src

=Abc.abc= は予想の証明につける予定の名前です。
リポジトリでは、この定理がライブラリに入り、 =#print axioms= が =propext= と =Classical.choice= と =Quot.sound= の3つだけを返したときに予想を証明したとみなすと決めています。

** 公理の監査
[[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Audit.lean][Audit.lean]] はライブラリのすべての定理に =#print axioms= を並べたファイルで、その出力を =audit.expected= に置いています。
=make check= はflakeの整形とMathlibのキャッシュの取得、 =lake build= を行ったあと、この出力を =audit.expected= と比べます。

#+begin_src console
$ nix develop --command make check
nix fmt -- --ci
traversed 22 files
emitted 1 files for processing
formatted 1 files (0 changed) in 1.06s
lake exe cache get
Current branch: HEAD
Using cache from origin: (some leanprover-community/mathlib4)
No files to download
Already decompressed 9031 file(s)
lake build
⚠ [9047/9052] Replayed Abc.Statement
warning: Abc/Statement.lean: imports `Mathlib` from package `mathlib`, which is designed for use with the module system; consider adding `module` to the start of this file
Build completed successfully (9052 jobs).
lake env lean Audit.lean | diff -u audit.expected -
#+end_src

最後の =diff= が何も出力せずに終わっているので、監査の出力は =audit.expected= と一致しています。

証明の途中に =sorry= が残っていると =#print axioms= の出力に =sorryAx= が出て比較が失敗します。
17個の定理がどれも3つの公理だけに依存していることを、この比較でCIでも確かめています。

** 証明に向けて
[[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/docs/roadmap.md][docs/roadmap.md]] には、このリポジトリの中でMathlibだけを使って進められる次の定理を並べています。

指数の $1 + \varepsilon$ を1にするとどの $K$ でも不等式が成り立たなくなることや、予想から十分大きな $n$ で $x^n + y^n = z^n$ に互いに素な正の解が無いことが導けることがその例です。
これらはどれも証明の方針を書いただけで、まだ定理にはなっていません。

リポジトリは [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound]] です。
Issue / PR大歓迎です。

* lean-abcbound: the open abc conjecture stated in Lean 4 against Mathlib, with theorems that check the statement
:properties:
:export_file_name: generated/contents/blog/2026/2eba97
:export_date: 2026-11-27 22:57
:export_updated: 2026-11-27 22:57
:export_lang: en
:export_original: /blog/2026/2f5c9f
:export_tags: lean mathlib formal-verification abc-conjecture release lean-abcbound
:export_draft: t
:end:
The abc conjecture is an open problem in number theory, and I made [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound][lean-abcbound]] to state it as a proposition in Lean 4 against Mathlib and to check with theorems that the proposition says what we intend.
Since the conjecture is still open, lean-abcbound holds the proposition =Abc.ABCConjecture= and theorems about how that proposition is written.

Lean's kernel checks only that a proof is a proof of the proposition it claims, so whether the proposition matches the conjecture is something people decide by reading it.
The theorems in lean-abcbound show that the proposition becomes false when you drop its coprimality hypothesis and that it is equivalent to the conjecture written in other forms, and they are the material for that decision.

The license is Apache-2.0, and the repository uses Lean v4.35.0 and Mathlib v4.35.0.
The code and output in this post come from [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/commit/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3][8ed08da]], the master branch at the time of writing.

[[github:conao3/lean-abcbound::Lean][The abc conjecture stated in Lean 4 against Mathlib]]

** The statement of the abc conjecture
For a positive integer $n$, $\mathrm{rad}(n)$ is the product of the distinct primes that divide $n$.
The abc conjecture compares $c$ with $\mathrm{rad}(abc)$ for coprime positive integers with $a + b = c$, and for $1 + 8 = 9$ we get $abc = 72 = 2^3 \cdot 3^2$, so $\mathrm{rad}(72) = 2 \cdot 3 = 6$ and $c = 9$ is larger.

[[./resources/public/img/2f5c9f-banner.png]]

The conjecture says that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a constant $K$ such that $c < K \cdot \mathrm{rad}(abc)^{1+\varepsilon}$ holds for every triple, and lean-abcbound writes this statement in [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Statement.lean#L12-L18][Abc/Statement.lean]] as follows.

#+begin_src lean
def rad (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, p

def ABCConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ a b c : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < b → a.Coprime b → a + b = c →
    (c : ℝ) < K * (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε)
#+end_src

=ABCConjecture= is a proposition (a =Prop=) defined with =def=.
The file imports Mathlib alone.

** Theorems that check the proposition says what we intend
The theorems that check how the proposition is written are in [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Sanity.lean][Abc/Sanity.lean]] and [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Equivalent.lean][Abc/Equivalent.lean]], and each of them says something about how the proposition is written and leaves the truth of the conjecture open.

*** Dropping the coprimality hypothesis makes it false
The theorem that negates =ABCConjecture= with only the =a.Coprime b= hypothesis removed is [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Sanity.lean#L21-L25][not_bound_without_coprime]].

#+begin_src lean
theorem not_bound_without_coprime :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ a b c : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < b → a + b = c →
      (c : ℝ) < K * (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε)
#+end_src

Every triple $2^n + 2^n = 2^{n+1}$ has $\mathrm{rad}(abc) = 2$, so $c$ can grow without bound, and the inequality fails for every $K$.

If I had left out the coprimality hypothesis when writing the proposition, it would have been a proposition whose negation Lean can prove.
This theorem shows that the hypothesis changes what the proposition means.

*** Equivalence with the conjecture written in other forms
The abc conjecture can be written in several forms, and DeepMind's [[https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/f606af160664c5a10952e9a957b100a1cd45bbeb/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/ABC.lean#L68-L75][formal-conjectures]] writes it in =abc.variants.lt_constant_mul= with the hypotheses that $c > 0$ and that every two of $a$, $b$, $c$ are coprime.
lean-abcbound copies these hypotheses into =ABCConjecturePairwise= and shows in [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Equivalent.lean#L44][abcConjecture_iff_pairwise]] that it is equivalent to =ABCConjecture=.

lean-abcbound does not import formal-conjectures, so I compared the hypotheses by reading the two files side by side.
The other theorem, [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Abc/Equivalent.lean#L107-L108][abcConjecture_iff_finite]], shows that =ABCConjecture= is equivalent to =ABCConjectureFinite=, the form that says for every $\varepsilon > 0$ only finitely many coprime triples satisfy $\mathrm{rad}(abc)^{1+\varepsilon} < c$.

#+begin_src lean
theorem abcConjecture_iff_pairwise : ABCConjecture ↔ ABCConjecturePairwise
theorem abcConjecture_iff_finite : ABCConjecture ↔ ABCConjectureFinite
#+end_src

Both theorems connect forms of the conjecture without proving any of them, so if any one of the three forms holds, the other two hold as well.

*** The definition of rad and concrete values
=rad_eq_radical= shows that =rad= agrees with Mathlib's =UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical= on the natural numbers.
Concrete values such as $\mathrm{rad}(12) = 6$ and $\mathrm{rad}(1 \cdot 8 \cdot 9) = 6$ are checks that the kernel computes with =decide +kernel=, and the repository keeps them apart from the universally quantified theorems.

** Checking it in Lean
Put the following =Demo.lean= at the root of the repository and pass it to =lake env lean=, and Lean prints the value of =rad 72=, the type of the proposition, and the axioms a theorem depends on.
The last line confirms that there is no theorem named =Abc.abc=.

#+begin_src lean
import Abc

#eval Abc.rad 72
#check Abc.ABCConjecture
#print axioms Abc.not_bound_without_coprime
#check Abc.abc
#+end_src

#+begin_src console
$ nix develop --command lake env lean Demo.lean
6
Abc.ABCConjecture : Prop
'Abc.not_bound_without_coprime' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
Demo.lean:6:7: error(lean.unknownIdentifier): Unknown identifier `Abc.abc`
#+end_src

=Abc.abc= is the name reserved for a proof of the conjecture.
The repository counts the conjecture as proved when this theorem is in the library and its =#print axioms= output lists =propext=, =Classical.choice=, and =Quot.sound= only.

** The axiom audit
[[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/Audit.lean][Audit.lean]] runs =#print axioms= on every theorem in the library, and =audit.expected= holds its output.
=make check= formats the flake, downloads the prebuilt Mathlib, runs =lake build=, and then compares this output with =audit.expected=.

#+begin_src console
$ nix develop --command make check
nix fmt -- --ci
traversed 22 files
emitted 1 files for processing
formatted 1 files (0 changed) in 1.06s
lake exe cache get
Current branch: HEAD
Using cache from origin: (some leanprover-community/mathlib4)
No files to download
Already decompressed 9031 file(s)
lake build
⚠ [9047/9052] Replayed Abc.Statement
warning: Abc/Statement.lean: imports `Mathlib` from package `mathlib`, which is designed for use with the module system; consider adding `module` to the start of this file
Build completed successfully (9052 jobs).
lake env lean Audit.lean | diff -u audit.expected -
#+end_src

The final =diff= printed nothing, so the audit output matches =audit.expected=.
A =sorry= left in a proof would add =sorryAx= to the =#print axioms= output and make the comparison fail.
CI runs the same comparison, which confirms that each of the 17 theorems depends on those three axioms only.

** Toward a proof
[[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound/blob/8ed08da1fac8268b64014e155874b91263acbad3/docs/roadmap.md][docs/roadmap.md]] lists the next theorems that can be worked on inside this repository with Mathlib alone.
Two examples are that the inequality fails for every $K$ once the exponent $1 + \varepsilon$ is replaced by 1, and that the conjecture implies $x^n + y^n = z^n$ has no coprime positive solutions for all large $n$.
Each of them has only a planned argument so far and is not yet a theorem.

The repository is at [[https://github.com/conao3/lean-abcbound]].
Issues and PRs are welcome.

* MELPAとGNU ELPAとGitHubのEmacsパッケージを1つの検索欄で探せるElisporeを作った
:properties:
:export_file_name: generated/contents/blog/2026/bed0c7
:export_date: 2026-11-27 23:23
:export_updated: 2026-11-27 23:23
:export_draft: t
:export_tags: emacs emacs-lisp melpa package-management release ts-elispore
:end:
MELPAとGNU ELPAとNonGNU ELPAに載っているEmacsパッケージも、GitHubに置いてあるだけのものも、1つの検索欄で探せるElisporeというサイトを作りました。
パッケージ名を打つとその名前がすでに使われているかが分かり、検索結果の行を開くとleafやuse-packageで入れる式と、MELPAの決まりに沿っているかを検査した結果が出ます。

サイトは [[https://elispore.conao3.com][elispore.conao3.com]] で、この記事を書いた時点で6,889件のパッケージを載せています。
載せているパッケージのカタログはGitHub Actionsが毎日作り直しています。

リポジトリは [[https://github.com/conao3/ts-elispore][conao3/ts-elispore]] で、ライセンスは [[https://github.com/conao3/ts-elispore/blob/b456119/LICENSE][Apache-2.0]] です。
この記事ではmasterの [[https://github.com/conao3/ts-elispore/commit/b456119][b456119]] と、2026-11-27に作り直したカタログを使いました。

[[github:conao3/ts-elispore::TypeScript][Find Emacs packages hosted on GitHub]]

** Elisporeでできること

- MELPAとGNU ELPAとNonGNU ELPAとGitHubのEmacsパッケージを、1つの検索欄で探す。
- =user:minad= や =stars:>=1000= のような修飾子で絞り込む。
- パッケージ名がカタログの中で使われているかを確かめる。
- leafかuse-packageの =:vc= でGitリポジトリから入れる式をコピーする。
- MELPAの決まりに沿っているかを、22個の必須のルールで検査した結果を見る。

** MELPAの審査を待たずにEmacsパッケージを探す

MELPAに新しいパッケージを載せるときはレシピをプルリクエストで送り、MELPAのメンテナーがパッケージを見て審査します。
[[https://github.com/melpa/melpa/blob/c906d3e4d5e04766a3656feffb2bcde941c4d25b/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?plain=1#L34][プルリクエストのテンプレート]] には次の確認の項目があります。

#+begin_quote
I understand the package must have been maintained in a public repository for 1 month or more
#+end_quote

AIを使って書いたパッケージについては、 [[https://github.com/melpa/melpa/blob/c906d3e4d5e04766a3656feffb2bcde941c4d25b/CONTRIBUTING.org?plain=1#L92-L95][CONTRIBUTING.org]] が次のように求めています。

#+begin_quote
Using AI to assist in writing your packages is not prohibited, but the human author must be the *first* and *most thorough* reviewer of any such output.
#+end_quote

AIを使うとパッケージを書く速さが上がるので、1つずつ人が審査する仕組みでは追いつかなくなると思っています。
機械で確かめられる決まりは機械で検査して、GitHubに置いたパッケージをそのまま探して入れられるようにしたいと考えて作りました。

Emacs Lispは名前空間が1つしかないので、MELPAの一覧はパッケージ名がすでに使われているかを調べるのにも役に立っていました。
ElisporeではGitHubにだけあるパッケージも含めて名前を調べられるようにしています。

** Emacsパッケージを名前で探す

[[./resources/public/img/bed0c7-search.png]]

検索欄に =leaf= と打つと、 =leaf= という名前のパッケージがすでにあることと、 =leaf= と =leaf-= で始まる名前のパッケージが合わせて7件あることが出ます。
名前が使われているかは絞り込みの条件によらずカタログ全体で確かめます。

その下には名前と説明とトピックが検索語に合う11件が並びます。
leaf.elの行にはGitHubのスター数557と19/19が出ていて、検査した必須のルール19個をすべて通したことを示しています。

検索欄には =source:gnu-elpa= や =user:minad= 、 =topic:completion= 、 =license:gpl-3.0= 、 =pushed:>=2026-01-01= 、 =stars:>=1000= のような修飾子も書けて、左の絞り込みで選んだ条件も検索欄の文字列に入ります。
検索欄の文字列はURLの =?q== にも入るので、例えば =user:minad stars:>=1000= でminadさんのorg-modernとverticoとconsultとcorfuの4件に絞り込んだ結果をURLで渡せます。

** leafやuse-packageで入れる式をコピーする

行を開くと、ライセンスや最後にpushした日時、載っている場所と一緒に、パッケージを入れる式が出ます。
式は初めはleafの形で、コードブロックの右上のボタンでuse-packageの形に切り替えられます。

GitHubにだけあるパッケージはリポジトリのURLを =:vc= に書いた式になります。
例えば [[https://s.conao3.com/blog/2026/7d9eba][vow]] の行には次の式が出ます。

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(leaf vow
  :vc (:url "https://github.com/conao3/vow.el"))
#+end_src

MELPAのレシピがあるパッケージでは、レシピのブランチと、リポジトリで確かめたLispのディレクトリが式に入ります。
magitはLispのファイルが =lisp/= にあるので、 =:lisp-dir= の付いた式になります。

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(leaf magit
  :vc (:url "https://github.com/magit/magit" :lisp-dir "lisp"))
#+end_src

leafの =:vc= はEmacs 29で入った [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Fetching-Package-Sources.html][package-vc]] でGitリポジトリからパッケージを入れるキーワードです。
この記事を書いた時点ではMELPAのleafで使えて、空の =user-emacs-directory= を使うEmacs 31.1にMELPAからleafを入れてこの2つの式を評価し、vowとmagitを読み込めることを確かめました。

use-packageの =:vc= はEmacs 30から使えます。
GNU ELPAかNonGNU ELPAに載っているパッケージはELPAの切り替えを選ぶと =:ensure t= の式になります。

** MELPAの決まりに沿っているかを検査する

[[./resources/public/img/bed0c7-checks.png]]

行を開くと、パッケージを検査した結果も出ます。

検査のルールはMELPAの [[https://github.com/melpa/melpa/blob/c906d3e4d5e04766a3656feffb2bcde941c4d25b/CONTRIBUTING.org][CONTRIBUTING.org]] と、CONTRIBUTING.orgが従うよう求めている [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/elisp/Tips.html][Emacs Lispの規約]] と、MELPAに出すパッケージの検査に使われている [[https://github.com/riscy/melpazoid][melpazoid]] から取っています。
どのルールにも出典の原文の引用を付けています。

必須のルールは22個でパッケージの点数になり、例えば =<package>.el= があることや、どのファイルも1行目で =lexical-binding= を有効にしていること、どのファイルも =;;; <file>.el ends here= の行で終わることなどを確かめます。
melpazoidのほかの検査84個は助言として並べ、点数には入れません。

ルールごとの説明と引用はサイトの [[https://elispore.conao3.com/about/#package-checks-about][ルールの一覧]] で読めます。
検査はパッケージのファイルを読むだけでEmacsで動かさないので、バイトコンパイルとcheckdocとpackage-lintは含みません。

同じパッケージでも載っている場所ごとに検査します。
leafはMELPAのバージョン20261122.915が19個のルールをすべて通していて、GNU ELPAのバージョン4.5.5は関数名を =#'= で渡すルールで落ちています。

GitHubのリポジトリだけで確かめるルールが3つと、MELPAのバージョンだけで確かめるルールが1つあるので、通ったルールの数の分母はMELPAで19、GNU ELPAで18になります。

検査するコマンドはRustで書いていて、必須のルールは [[https://s.conao3.com/blog/2026/23d62c][leanfran]] を使ってLeanで定義し、Rustのコードにしています。
GitHubのリポジトリを手元で検査するときは、 =owner/repo= を1行に1つ書いたファイルを渡します。

#+begin_src sh
$ printf 'conao3/leaf.el\nconao3/flylint.el\n' > repos.txt
$ nix run github:conao3/ts-elispore#checker -- \
    --source github --github-list repos.txt --output checks.json | head -n 1
Packages: 2; errors: 0; cached: 0; downloaded: 2
$ jq '.results | map_values(.failed)' checks.json
{
  "github/conao3/flylint.el": [
    "provide",
    "footer"
  ],
  "github/conao3/leaf.el": [
    "mz-have-you-done-the-paperwork-to"
  ]
}
#+end_src

flylintはテストで使うファイル =flylint-tests-flylint.el= に =provide= が無く、最後の行が =;;; flylint-tests.el ends here= になっているので、2つの必須のルールで落ちました。

GitHubのleaf.elは必須のルールをすべて通っています。
著作権をFSFに譲渡したGNU ELPAのパッケージなので、著作権の表示にmelpazoidの「Have you done the paperwork to assign this copyright?」の助言が付きます。

[[https://s.conao3.com/blog/2026/a80aa6][Vercel Boardで組んだソフトウェア工場]] では、私のEmacsパッケージ20個をこの検査にかける仕事を、パッケージごとのタスク20件に分けて動かしました。

** カタログに載るEmacsパッケージ

カタログはGitHubの検索とMELPAとGNU ELPAとNonGNU ELPAから毎日作り直します。
フォークや設定ファイルの集まり、awesomeの一覧は外し、直下か =lisp/= に =.el= のファイルがあるリポジトリだけを載せます。

GitHubの検索では、スターが20以上のEmacs Lispのリポジトリをスターの多い順に400件まで読みます。
トピック =emacs-package= のリポジトリと、2026-01-01より後にpushされたEmacs Lispのリポジトリはそれぞれ200件まで読み、ほかのトピックのリポジトリも加えます。

MELPAに載っていない自分のパッケージをカタログに載せたいときは、フォークでない公開のリポジトリの直下か =lisp/= に =.el= のファイルを置き、リポジトリにトピック =emacs-package= を付けます。
=emacs-package= の検索はスターの多い順に200件までなので、トピックを付けても載らないことがあります。

* Elispore: search Emacs packages from MELPA, GNU ELPA and GitHub in one search box
:properties:
:export_file_name: generated/contents/blog/2026/48ea25
:export_date: 2026-11-27 23:23
:export_updated: 2026-11-27 23:23
:export_draft: t
:export_lang: en
:export_original: /blog/2026/bed0c7
:export_tags: emacs emacs-lisp melpa package-management release ts-elispore
:end:
I built Elispore, a site where one search box finds Emacs packages from MELPA, GNU ELPA and NonGNU ELPA, and packages that only live on GitHub.
When you type a package name, it tells you whether the name is taken, and when you open a row in the results, you get a leaf or use-package form to install the package and the results of checks against MELPA's rules.

The site runs at [[https://elispore.conao3.com][elispore.conao3.com]] and lists 6,889 packages as of this writing.
GitHub Actions rebuilds its catalog of packages every day.

The repository is [[https://github.com/conao3/ts-elispore][conao3/ts-elispore]], under the [[https://github.com/conao3/ts-elispore/blob/b456119/LICENSE][Apache-2.0]] license.
For this post I used [[https://github.com/conao3/ts-elispore/commit/b456119][b456119]] on master and the catalog rebuilt on 2026-11-27.

[[github:conao3/ts-elispore::TypeScript][Find Emacs packages hosted on GitHub]]

** What you can do with Elispore

- Search Emacs packages from MELPA, GNU ELPA, NonGNU ELPA and GitHub in one search box.
- Narrow the results with qualifiers such as =user:minad= and =stars:>=1000=.
- Check whether a package name is taken in the catalog.
- Copy a leaf or use-package form that installs the package from its Git repository with =:vc=.
- See the results of checks against 22 required rules that follow MELPA's guidelines.

** Finding Emacs packages without waiting for MELPA's review

To add a new package to MELPA, you send its recipe in a pull request, and MELPA's maintainers look at the package and review it.
The [[https://github.com/melpa/melpa/blob/c906d3e4d5e04766a3656feffb2bcde941c4d25b/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?plain=1#L34][pull request template]] has this item on its checklist:

#+begin_quote
I understand the package must have been maintained in a public repository for 1 month or more
#+end_quote

For packages written with AI, [[https://github.com/melpa/melpa/blob/c906d3e4d5e04766a3656feffb2bcde941c4d25b/CONTRIBUTING.org?plain=1#L92-L95][CONTRIBUTING.org]] asks for this:

#+begin_quote
Using AI to assist in writing your packages is not prohibited, but the human author must be the *first* and *most thorough* reviewer of any such output.
#+end_quote

AI lets people write packages faster, so I think a process where people review each package by hand will fall behind.
I built Elispore so that machines check the rules a machine can check, and so that you can find a package on GitHub and install it from there.

Emacs Lisp has a single namespace, so the MELPA list also helped people check whether a package name was taken.
Elispore lets you check names against packages that exist only on GitHub as well.

** Searching Emacs packages by name

[[./resources/public/img/bed0c7-search.png]]

When you type =leaf= in the search box, Elispore says that a package named =leaf= exists and that 7 packages are named =leaf= or start with =leaf-=.
It checks the name against the whole catalog, whatever filters you have selected.

Below that, the 11 packages whose name, description or topics match the query appear.
The leaf.el row shows 557 GitHub stars and 19/19, which means it passed all 19 required rules that apply.

The search box also takes qualifiers such as =source:gnu-elpa=, =user:minad=, =topic:completion=, =license:gpl-3.0=, =pushed:>=2026-01-01= and =stars:>=1000=, and the filters you select on the left appear in the query too.
The query goes into the URL as =?q==, so you can share a filtered result by its URL, for example =user:minad stars:>=1000=, which lists minad's org-modern, vertico, consult and corfu.

** Copying a leaf or use-package form

When you open a row, you see the license, the date of the last push and the sources that list the package, next to a form that installs it.
The form starts in leaf style, and the button at the top right of the code block switches it to use-package.

For a package that exists only on GitHub, the form puts the repository URL in =:vc=.
The row for [[https://s.conao3.com/blog/2026/aeda19][vow]] shows this form:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(leaf vow
  :vc (:url "https://github.com/conao3/vow.el"))
#+end_src

For a package with a MELPA recipe, the form includes the recipe's branch and the Lisp directory that Elispore confirmed in the repository.
magit keeps its Lisp files in =lisp/=, so its form has =:lisp-dir=.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(leaf magit
  :vc (:url "https://github.com/magit/magit" :lisp-dir "lisp"))
#+end_src

leaf's =:vc= keyword installs a package from its Git repository with [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Fetching-Package-Sources.html][package-vc]], which arrived in Emacs 29.
As of this writing, the leaf on MELPA supports it: I installed leaf from MELPA into Emacs 31.1 with an empty =user-emacs-directory=, evaluated these two forms, and loaded vow and magit.

use-package has =:vc= from Emacs 30.
For a package in GNU ELPA or NonGNU ELPA, the ELPA switch gives you a form with =:ensure t=.

** Checking packages against MELPA's rules

[[./resources/public/img/bed0c7-checks.png]]

An open row also shows the results of the package checks.

The rules come from MELPA's [[https://github.com/melpa/melpa/blob/c906d3e4d5e04766a3656feffb2bcde941c4d25b/CONTRIBUTING.org][CONTRIBUTING.org]], the [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/elisp/Tips.html][Emacs Lisp conventions]] that CONTRIBUTING.org asks packages to follow, and [[https://github.com/riscy/melpazoid][melpazoid]], which people use to check packages before they submit them to MELPA.
Each rule quotes the source text it comes from.

The 22 required rules make up a package's score, and they check, for example, that =<package>.el= exists, that every file enables =lexical-binding= on its first line, and that every file ends with a =;;; <file>.el ends here= line.
Elispore lists melpazoid's other 84 checks as advice, and they do not count toward the score.

The [[https://elispore.conao3.com/about/#package-checks-about][list of rules]] on the site explains each rule with its quotes.
The checks only read the package files and do not run them in Emacs, so they leave out byte compilation, checkdoc and package-lint.

Elispore checks a package once for each source that lists it.
For leaf, the MELPA version 20261122.915 passes all 19 rules, and the GNU ELPA version 4.5.5 fails the rule about passing function names with =#'=.

Elispore runs three rules only on GitHub repositories and one rule only on MELPA versions, so the count is out of 19 for MELPA and out of 18 for GNU ELPA.

The checker is a command written in Rust, and I defined its required rules in Lean and turned them into Rust code with [[https://s.conao3.com/blog/2026/21ebbd][leanfran]].
To check GitHub repositories on your machine, pass it a file with one =owner/repo= per line.

#+begin_src sh
$ printf 'conao3/leaf.el\nconao3/flylint.el\n' > repos.txt
$ nix run github:conao3/ts-elispore#checker -- \
    --source github --github-list repos.txt --output checks.json | head -n 1
Packages: 2; errors: 0; cached: 0; downloaded: 2
$ jq '.results | map_values(.failed)' checks.json
{
  "github/conao3/flylint.el": [
    "provide",
    "footer"
  ],
  "github/conao3/leaf.el": [
    "mz-have-you-done-the-paperwork-to"
  ]
}
#+end_src

flylint fails two required rules because its test helper file =flylint-tests-flylint.el= has no =provide= and its last line reads =;;; flylint-tests.el ends here=.

The leaf.el repository on GitHub passes all the required rules.
It is a GNU ELPA package whose copyright belongs to the FSF, so its copyright notice gets melpazoid's advice "Have you done the paperwork to assign this copyright?"

In the [[https://s.conao3.com/blog/2026/048a8b][software factory I built on Vercel Board]], I ran 20 of my Emacs packages through these checks as 20 tasks, one per package.

** Emacs packages in the catalog

Elispore rebuilds the catalog every day from GitHub search, MELPA, GNU ELPA and NonGNU ELPA.
It leaves out forks, collections of configuration files and awesome lists, and keeps only repositories with an =.el= file at the root or in =lisp/=.

From GitHub search it reads up to 400 Emacs Lisp repositories with 20 or more stars, most starred first.
It also reads up to 200 repositories with the =emacs-package= topic and up to 200 Emacs Lisp repositories pushed after 2026-01-01, and adds repositories with a few other topics.

To get your own package into the catalog when it is not on MELPA, put an =.el= file at the root or in =lisp/= of a public repository that is not a fork, and add the =emacs-package= topic to the repository.
The =emacs-package= search reads only the 200 most starred repositories, so the topic alone may not get your package listed.
